name: Disturbance recorder
summary: Recorder that captures analogue waveforms and binary signals before and after a trigger for fault analysis.
description: A disturbance recorder captures sampled current and voltage waveforms together with breaker and protection contact states when a trigger occurs. Pre-fault and post-fault data let engineers check how protection performed, so the recorder is drawn with its analogue inputs from CTs and VTs and its binary inputs from trip and position contacts.

Many protection relays now include this function, so a separate recorder symbol usually indicates a dedicated substation-wide unit. The symbol does not show trigger conditions, sample rate or record length, and records are commonly exchanged in a standard file format that should be named in the specification.
readingNotes: Trace analogue inputs to their CTs and VTs.
List binary inputs and their sources.
distinction: A disturbance recorder stores high-rate waveforms around an event; a sequence-of-events recorder stores timestamped contact changes only.
